history_note: The initial workflow did not retain an exhaustive candidate/omission list. This register records the actual included cases and their comparison rationale; it does not reconstruct an exhaustive screen.
outside_scope: Other catalogue families are outside this contrastive selection; no frequency, dominance or representativeness inference over the full release is made.
assessment_axes: newly proposed bridge and exact parameter dependence

cases.included_for: A comparison of ordinary, logarithmic, and exceptional-scale quantifiers with an identifiable finite-law transfer.
cases.input: Shared-prime residue graph and signed trace observables.
cases.target: Ordinary binary cancellation at every cutoff for fixed affine forms.
cases.preserved_property: Arithmetic dependence among translated residues and a signed saving.
cases.quantifiers: Fixed forms before cutoff growth; one fixed factor before every character and growing-twist infimum.
cases.loss_budget: Uniform costs as prime-supply count grows like log log X.
cases.contrastive_boundary: Logarithmic or exceptional-scale control alone does not give every-cutoff control.

cases.included_for: An optimal endpoint proposed through a centre-uniform geometric/arithmetic bridge.
cases.input: Logarithmic-curve jets and rational-Gaussian interpolation minors.
cases.target: Every exponent nu>2 is eventually excluded as a rational-approximation exponent.
cases.preserved_property: Ordinary jet surjectivity and a nonzero determinant after denominator clearing.
cases.quantifiers: Weights are selected before approximation centres; thresholds may depend on centres.
cases.loss_budget: Degree-growth exponent m+1 versus m for transverse classes, coupled to collision savings.
cases.contrastive_boundary: Counting dimensions or selecting weights after seeing centres does not supply the stated interface.

cases.included_for: Two different sharp geometric routes, with analytic, finite, and rigidity interfaces.
cases.input: Boundary feasibility for symmetric strip bodies; dual-cone Gaussian layers for general bodies.
cases.target: Sharp volume-product lower bounds and equality classification in all dimensions.
cases.preserved_property: Exact normalizations, disjoint simplex accounting, and an all-real scalar error inequality.
cases.quantifiers: All dimensions; every segment and limiting body, with equality handled separately.
cases.loss_budget: Feasibility mass and matrix/layer/commutator errors must fit the sharp constant.
cases.contrastive_boundary: A conformal lens or positive finite nodes needs the transfer and continuum extension.

cases.included_for: A contrast between a full-gap upgrade, sufficient restricted control, and exact-law cost conversion.
cases.input: Enlarged matching products, paired matroid defects, and padded table completions.
cases.target: General matching/common-base FPRAS; exact arbitrary-margin uniform sampling.
cases.preserved_property: Full product control or explicitly sufficient observables/returns; the actual output law.
cases.quantifiers: Explicit input/oracles; worst-case tape bounds versus expected exact bit work; variable table dimensions.
cases.loss_budget: Replication and comparison polynomials; fresh warm restarts; exponentially expensive input-law tabulation with polynomial precision dependence.
cases.contrastive_boundary: A restricted gap does not give full mixing; accuracy alone does not make exact correction affordable.
cases.inherited_framework: Partition-restricted Poincare control and stationary empirical-average estimates have a directly credited antecedent in Chen, Vigoda and Yang (2026); the candidate common-base gain is its matroid-specific transport/trace/warm-start realization.

cases.included_for: A proposed qualitative hardness jump from imperfect to near-one completeness.
cases.input: Latent nonlinear observable, linear lifts, shortcode transfer and advice-restricted decoding.
cases.target: Deterministic polynomial reductions with completeness 1-epsilon and soundness delta.
cases.preserved_property: Noise-response separation and permitted information for each decoded strategy.
cases.quantifiers: Each fixed error pair precedes alphabet selection; alphabet is independent of instance size.
cases.loss_budget: Soundness under adaptive lifts and repetition without eroding near-one completeness.
cases.contrastive_boundary: Ordinary repetition and an inherited inverse theorem do not themselves remove the completeness barrier.

cases.included_for: A finite-field contrast to real/operator positivity and a defect-preserving algebraic construction.
cases.input: Characteristic-two incidence pairings, local groups, rectangular inverses and square packing.
cases.target: Scalar a,b in a genuine group algebra with ab=1 and ba!=1.
cases.preserved_property: The reverse defect and local subgroup embeddings.
cases.quantifiers: An actual finite field/group/witness, with primitive ell-th roots and stated incidence constraints.
cases.loss_budget: Regular high-girth construction, size inequality and compatible character packing.
cases.contrastive_boundary: Real positive semidefinite reasoning changes the coefficient field; an abstract rank defect needs realization in the group algebra.

cases.included_for: A sharp endpoint whose complete scope distinguishes it from scalar and small-base claims.
cases.input: Ordered Fourier/Gram coefficient tests; structural ordered density comparison controlling the optimal similarity metric.
cases.target: Constant two for all base and coefficient dimensions.
cases.preserved_property: Noncommuting product order and a common bound under matrix amplification.
cases.quantifiers: Independent arbitrary base n and coefficient m; independent matrix-valued tests.
cases.loss_budget: Sharp diagonal/cross estimates with no coefficient-dimension factor.
cases.contrastive_boundary: Entrywise scalar bounds incur m; classical similarity does not establish the sharp complete bound.

cases.included_for: Signed cancellation with an explicit scale-uniform budget needed for a global conclusion.
cases.input: Retarded signed force along source/receiver characteristics.
cases.target: Large-data global smooth solutions without symmetry in the stated class.
cases.preserved_property: Receiver energy band and constants uniform over compact solution prefixes and momentum scales.
cases.quantifiers: Fixed datum/horizon before dyadic P and the compact prefix; band holds throughout the interval.
cases.loss_budget: Logarithmic momentum growth permits harmonic divergence of doubling times.
cases.contrastive_boundary: Taking absolute values too early discards signed cancellation. A loss with convergent reciprocal dyadic-scale series does not suffice for this continuation inference; slightly superlogarithmic losses can still satisfy the divergence test.
